cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I send the workshop closure notice, name who backed your decision. 'Management' is not an adequate attribution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the approver. Who supported the proposal? Please don't collapse two different questions into one name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but leave them out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then list Sales as both supporter and beneficiary. Who authorised the space transfer? I need that name before this goes to the staff.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 attribution, A3 approver-versus-supporter and A5 beneficiary plus transfer authorisation apply professional precision to revealing backers.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 director approval and B4 Sales support/benefit are compatible; A5 asks separate transfer authorisation without assuming a new person.

relationship.evidence: B2 urgency and B4 leave-Sales-out request give real resistance to full disclosure.

heightening.evidence: B4 floor-space gain causes A5 beneficiary classification and signoff question.

specificity.evidence: A1 workshop closure and B4 space transfer make affected people and benefit concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 document entry and final authority question both respond to B disclosure without a concluding sermon.
